title: Hourglass launch cadence and decision crib — Nov 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose
Quick compact run-through for a staggered, throttled release (the "hourglass" cadence): keep early traffic narrow and high-observability, then widen after 24h if signals are clean. This is a compact crib for on-call, release leads, and SREs. Treat as a living sketch — copy into the live launch doc before go-time.

Goals
- Validate canary in prod with representative workloads (chat, embeddings spike)
- Maintain 99th P50 latency targets; surface regressions within 5 minutes
- Keep error budget consumption < 1% in first 72h (target < 0.5%)
- Zero customer-impacting incidents (SEV2+); if any, immediate rollback to previous stable variant

High level approach (hourglass metaphor)
- Narrow neck (0–6h): 1%–5% traffic, verbose tracing, low batch sizes, no batching optimizations, KV cache warm-up disabled for experimental model variants
- Widening cone (6–24h): ramp to 20% if all gates pass, re-enable conservative KV cache, increase batch thresholds slightly
- Full glass (24–72h): expand to 100% traffic with monitored gradual backfill and soft-throttle rules; optimistic batching and quantized variant enabled only after stability window

Roles and quick contacts
- Release lead: Marcus Chen (owner) — pager: pagerduty:marcus, slack DMs
- SRE lead: Leah Ortiz — runbook arbiter for throttles and infra actions
- Prod-SWE oncall: rotating (see oncall schedule)
- Console/Telemetry owner: Priya Nair — will manage dashboards and alert tuning
- Rollback authority: Engineering manager on call (Tomás Rivera if unclear)

Preflight checklist (copy to preflight Confluence + handoff)
- [ ] Green CI for release branch (PR#4521 merged, smoke tests pass)
- [ ] Canary image built, sha256 pinned in deploy manifest
- [ ] Capacity reservation confirmed (dedicated nodes reserved for 12h post-release)
- [ ] Coordinated calendar invite sent to SRE, Release, Product, CS (24h watch rota)
- [ ] Slack channel created: #deploy-hourglass-2026-11-05 (invitees above)
- [ ] External customers on dedicated capacity notified (if impacted)
- [ ] Key feature flags set to OFF by default for non-experiment cohorts
- [ ] Telemetry knobs: set sample rate=1 for tracing on canary routes; metrics retention snapshot for 72h
- [ ] Rollback playbook copied to channel and pinned

Minute-by-minute / hour-by-hour compact calendar (first 72h)
- T-60 to T0: final gates check; all leads on call; notify #deploy-channel; snapshot dashboards; note baseline metrics (error rate, p50/p95/p99, token/sec)
- T0 (deploy start): push canary 0.1 (1% traffic), start verbose tracing, start smoke tests runbook
- 0–15m: confirm canary health (liveness/probes OK), smoke test 1 (auth, inference simple prompt, streaming), confirm no 5xx in logs
- 15–60m: observe for latency drift; if p99 > baseline + 50ms or errors > 0.5% -> throttle to 0% and rollback plan trigger
- 1–3h: if healthy, step canary to 5%; enable prefix caching read-only to validate cache behavior (no writes yet)
- 3–6h: if stable, step to 10% and re-enable conservative batcher (batch_size cap = 8 tokens)
- 6–12h: if stable, open to 20% with sampling of long-context requests; run stress-window test for embeddings endpoint
- 12–24h: widen toward 50% if telemetry stable; enable write-path cache warming; gradually permit quantized variant for low-risk routes only
- 24h gate: comprehensive signal check (see decision gates below). If pass, authorize full rollout to 100% across regions over next 6–12h with soft-throttle ramps per region
- 24–72h: monitor at 15m cadence for first 12h, then 1h cadence; evening/night watch rotation begins at 24h; ticket retro stub created at 48h

Decision gates (automated + human)
- Safety metrics snapshot (automated every 5m):
  - Error rate (5xx or inference failures) over 5m window must be < 0.5%
  - Token-production drop: if total tokens/sec drops below 80% baseline -> investigate immediately
  - Latency: p99 must not exceed baseline p99 + 100ms for more than 3 consecutive windows
  - Resource saturation: GPU utilization > 90% for 10m -> throttle and investigate
- Human approval required at: 6h, 24h, 48h for any widening action beyond automated ramp. Release lead + SRE lead must confirm in thread that postmortems not required and telemetry is green.

Throttle gate quick recipes
- Soft-throttle: reduce traffic target by 50% (e.g., 20% -> 10%) and notify channel; increase sampling for traces; collect heap/stack dumps from impacted nodes
- Hard-throttle: cut traffic to 0% (equivalent to rollback trigger) and start rollback runbook; contact rollback authority
- Local mitigation: spin extra warm nodes and redirect traffic regionally (only if capacity reserved)

Rollback criteria (fast and non-ambiguous)
- Any SEV1/SEV2 incident linked to new variant -> immediate rollback to previous canary/variant and declare incident bridge
- Consistent latency regression where p99 > baseline + 200ms for 30m -> rollback recommended
- Error rate spike > 1% for more than 10m despite throttling and mitigations -> rollback

Smoke + validation checklist (automation!)
- End-to-end simple prompt -> expected token prefix + sanity hash match
- Streaming connection up to 60s -> no mid-stream resets
- Embedding vector shape and sample cosine sanity check against golden set
- Function-call structured output: validate JSON schema against toy prompts
- Multi-turn KV cache test: ensure no leakage across requests (privacy check)

Telemetry and dashboards to watch (links pinned in #deploy-channel)
- Inference-latency (P50/P95/P99) by region and model variant
- Error-rate by route and token position
- Token/sec production (by model & region)
- GPU memory/temperature/utilization per cluster
- Queue/backlog length for batching subsystem

Communications plan
- T0 announcement: #deploy-hourglass-2026-11-05 with timestamp + short summary
- On any gated decision or rollback: @channel in deploy Slack, 1-line status update in #incidents if SEV2+
- Customer-facing comms: CS lead prepares templated message if 1) rollback affects any customer-deployed variants or 2) broader outage. Keep message short, status-first.

Post-release notes (to prepare during 24–48h)
- Short release notes draft (for internal & external): bullets of user-visible changes, known limitations (if any), mitigations performed, expected follow-ups (telemetry retention, perf tuning)
- Owners assigned for follow-ups: perf tweaks, batching tuning, documentation updates

Draft release notes (internal first pass)
- New canary variant for model X with optimized attention kernel (experimental quantized path for low-cost routes).
- Improved batching heuristics for short-sequence chat workloads (configurable per-route).
- Fixed a memory-bleed issue when handling large KV cache keys (regression fix).
- Notes: quantized variant disabled by default in full rollout until 48h green window completed.

Open questions / notes to self (unresolved)
- Need to confirm exact cap for batch_size on region eu-west-1 during initial ramp (Ops reserved different instance types). Leah to confirm by EOD T-1.
- Do we want prefix-caching writes on at 12h or 24h? Current sketch says 12h read-only, 24h writes. Team preference?
- Add a small synthetic workload that simulates multi-turn streaming under network jitter — we have a test but need to integrate into smoke automation.

Retro prompts (post 72h)
- What signals were most predictive of issues? (latency p99, error spike, token/sec drop?)
- Did any mitigation pathways add risk (e.g., enabling cache writes while batcher still warming)?
- Time-to-detect and time-to-recover metrics collection: extract from alert logs

Quick appendices (snippets to paste into live runbook)
- Rollback command (kubernetes): kubectl set image deployment/inference inference=image:stable-sha --record ; kubectl rollout status deployment/inference -w
- Soft-throttle directive (traffic manager): trafficctl set-target inference-route --percent 10 --variant stable

-- end crib --

Notes: keep this in the shared drive as the canonical short-form for the hourglass cadence. Copy into the deployment ticket (REL-2176) before T-0 and paste the live telemetry links. If anything deviates from the above, annotate immediately in the channel.
